entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus was a Roman Senator who played a pivotal role in the Roman Empire during the 2nd and 3rd centuries AD.

He was one of the 200 senators who participated in the Roman Senate's deliberations on the Edict of Marcus Aurelius, a comprehensive codification of Roman law that aimed to bring justice and stability to the empire.

As an ordinary consul for the year 197, Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus worked alongside Cuspius Rufinus to govern the Roman provinces and maintain the empire's extensive borders.

Despite his modest stature, Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus left a lasting legacy in the annals of Roman history, demonstrating the importance of senatorial involvement in shaping the empire's policies and institutions.

His remarkable experience, though lesser-known among the general public, serves as a testament to the vital role that ordinary Romans like Titus Sextius Magius Lateranus played in the intricate web of imperial governance.
